Confidential computing encrypts data while it is being processed, narrowing the window in which information is exposed. Access controls and transparency logs aim to give customers visibility into, and in some cases the ability to approve or deny, administrative access by the provider. Together these tools are meant to support the principle that a provider's commercial location need not dictate who can ultimately reach the data.

The second pillar, compliance, concerns alignment with the EU's expanding body of digital regulation. This includes long-standing rules such as the General Data Protection Regulation, alongside newer frameworks like the Data Act, the NIS2 directive on cybersecurity, and the still-evolving European cybersecurity certification scheme for cloud services. Providers are likely to face pressure to demonstrate conformity with these requirements in verifiable ways, and Google's positioning suggests it intends to map its controls and certifications to them rather than treat compliance as an afterthought.

The third pillar, cooperation, reflects a model in which global hyperscalers work alongside European companies

ce80a3fa0e1e6dc4.bodyJa:
NVIDIAが昨年のGTC Paris at VivaTechで打ち出した欧州AI構想から約1年。フランスがその公約を着実に実行へ移していることが、NVIDIAの最新報告で示された。AIファクトリーの整備や国家規模の計算基盤の拡充、オープンなフロンティアモデルの開発が並行して進み、欧州のAI競争力を左右する試金石として関心を集めている。

ここで言うAIファクトリーとは、大規模なAIモデルの学習や推論に特化したデータセンターを指す。従来の汎用的なデータセンターと異なり、GPUを高密度に集積し、ネットワークや電力供給、冷却に至るまでAI処理に最適化した設計が特徴とされる。フランスはこうした施設を国内に展開することで、海外のクラウド事業者に過度に依存せず、自国でAI開発を完結させる「デジタル主権」の確立を目指していると見られる。

計算基盤の拡充は、研究機関やスタートアップが大規模モデルを訓練するための前提となる。フランスにはMistral AIのように世界的な注目を集める企業も育っており、国家レベルの計算資源とオープンなモデル開発を結びつけることで、米国の大手や中国勢に対抗しうる独自の生態系を築こうとしている。重みや技術仕様を広く共有するオープンなフロンティアモデルには、欧州域内での応用や安全性の検証を促す狙いがあるとみられる。

背景には、生成AIの基盤技術が一部の米国企業に集中することへの欧州の警戒感がある。EUはAI規制法(AI Act)の整備を進める一方、産業面では計算能力の確保が急務となっている。NVIDIA製GPUは現在のAI開発で事実上の標準的な存在となっており、その供給と各国の投資の規模が今後の勢力図を左右する可能性がある。

フランスの動きは、ドイツや他の加盟国による同様の取り組みとあわせ、欧州全体のAI戦略の方向性を占う材料となりそうだ。もっとも、巨額のインフラ投資や電力確保、半導体供給の制約といった課題も残されており、構想がどこまで実体を伴うかは今後の進捗を見極める必要がある。発表から1年という節目は、計画の実行力が問われる段階に入ったことを示しているといえる。
ce80a3fa0e1e6dc4.bodyEn:
A year after NVIDIA used its GTC event in Paris, held alongside the VivaTech conference, to outline a sweeping vision for European artificial intelligence, France appears to be turning many of those commitments into concrete infrastructure. The country is pressing ahead with so-called AI factories, expanding national compute capacity, and supporting the development of open frontier models built on NVIDIA hardware and software. The progress matters because it offers an early test of whether Europe can build sovereign AI capability rather than relying primarily on systems and data centers operated outside the continent.

The term "AI factory" refers to a data center purpose-built for the full lifecycle of modern AI, from training large models on vast datasets to running them at scale for inference. Unlike a general-purpose data center, an AI factory is organized around dense clusters of accelerators, high-bandwidth networking, and specialized cooling, with the explicit goal of turning raw data and electricity into trained models and usable predictions. France's push in this area reflects a broader European interest in keeping the physical and computational layer of AI closer to home, where it can be governed by local regulation and data-protection rules such as the EU's GDPR and the recently phased-in AI Act.

National compute capacity is the second pillar of the strategy. Building large GPU clusters domestically gives researchers, startups, and public institutions access to the hardware needed to train competitive models without waiting in line for capacity on overseas cloud platforms. France has historically been active here through initiatives like the Jean Zay supercomputer, and the current expansion appears to build on that foundation. NVIDIA's role centers on its accelerated computing platform, including its GPUs and the surrounding software ecosystem such as CUDA, networking technology from its Mellanox and Spectrum lines, and reference designs that partners use to assemble large systems. Cloud and infrastructure providers in France and across Europe are among the operators standing up this capacity.

Open frontier models represent the third and perhaps most closely watched element. Frontier models are the largest and most capable systems at the leading edge of the field, and "open" generally signals that model weights or substantial technical details are released publicly, allowing others to study, fine-tune, and deploy them. France is home to Mistral AI, one of the more prominent European model developers, and the country's emphasis on openness aligns with a wider argument that transparency can support safety research, competition, and adoption by smaller organizations. It is worth noting that "open" exists on a spectrum, and the exact licensing terms of any given model determine how freely it can actually be used commercially.

The context behind these moves is a continent-wide effort to reduce dependence on a small number of foreign technology suppliers while still drawing on their hardware. European policymakers have repeatedly framed AI infrastructure as a matter of economic competitiveness and strategic autonomy, and the European Union has floated large funding programs aimed at AI and supercomputing, including the EuroHPC joint undertaking that has financed several of the region's most powerful machines. France's national activity sits within that framework, complementing rather than replacing the broader EU agenda.

Several caveats temper the optimism. AI factories are energy intensive, and scaling them raises questions about power availability and sustainability, though France's substantial nuclear generation gives it a relatively low-carbon electricity base compared with some neighbors. There is also the practical challenge that the most advanced accelerators remain in high demand globally, which can constrain how quickly any country expands capacity. And while domestic compute and open models strengthen local capability, much of the underlying chip technology is still designed and manufactured through international supply chains.

Taken together, the developments suggest France is positioning itself as a focal point for European AI ambitions, pairing public and private investment with NVIDIA's commercial platform. Whether this translates into models and applications that compete at the global frontier will likely depend on sustained funding, talent retention, and the speed at which the new infrastructure comes online. For now, the trajectory indicates that the announcements made in Paris a year ago were not merely aspirational, and that the broader European bid for AI self-reliance is moving from rhetoric toward operational reality.

cb7b2d32993f347e.bodyJa:
ローカルで大規模言語モデル（LLM）を手軽に動かせるツール「Ollama」が、バージョン0.30.10を公開した。今回のアップデートは、Apple Silicon向け推論エンジン「MLX」への対応拡充が中心で、新たな対応モデルの追加と基盤エンジンの更新が柱となっている。

最大の変更点は、「Command A」および「North」ファミリーのモデルが、Apple Silicon上でMLXエンジンを用いて動作するようになったことだ。MLXはAppleが開発する機械学習フレームワークで、M系チップが備えるユニファイドメモリ（統合メモリ）アーキテクチャを活かし、CPUとGPUが同一のメモリ空間を共有する設計に最適化されている。これにより、MacのハードウェアでLLMを動かす際に、メモリ効率や推論速度の面で利点が期待できるとされる。

Ollamaはこれまで、主にC/C++製の定番推論ライブラリ「llama.cpp」をバックエンドとして採用してきたが、近年はMLXエンジンを併用する形でApple Silicon環境での最適化を進めている。今回のリリースでも、基盤となるllama.cppエンジンがbuild 9672へと更新されており、両エンジンの並行強化が続いていることがうかがえる。あわせて、MLX向けのビルド成果物（build artifacts）に関する不具合の修正も含まれている。

Command Aは、Cohereが企業向け用途を想定して開発したモデルとして知られる。こうした比較的新しいオープンモデルがローカル環境でも扱えるようになる流れは、開発者にとって選択肢の拡大を意味する。クラウドAPIに依存せず手元のマシンで推論を完結できる点は、データをローカルに保持したいユースケースやコスト面で利点がある一方、モデルの規模によっては相応のメモリやストレージが必要になる可能性がある。

ローカルLLMの分野では、OllamaのほかにもLM StudioやGPT4Allといったツールが利用者を広げており、各ツールがApple Siliconへの最適化やモデル対応の幅を競っている状況だ。Ollamaの今回の更新は、こうした競争のなかでMac環境での使い勝手を着実に高める一歩と位置づけられる。詳細な変更点は公式のチェンジログで確認できる。
cb7b2d32993f347e.bodyEn:
Ollama has published version 0.30.10, a maintenance-focused update to its popular local large language model runtime that centers on improved support for Apple Silicon hardware. The release matters because it expands the set of models that can run efficiently on Mac computers using Apple's native machine learning stack, while keeping the project's underlying inference engines current. For users who prefer to run models on their own machines rather than through cloud APIs, incremental releases like this one steadily reduce the gap between local and hosted performance.

The headline change is that Command A and the North family of models can now run on Apple Silicon through Ollama's MLX engine. Command A is a high-capability instruction-tuned model associated with Cohere's lineup, and the North family appears to be drawn from the same ecosystem of enterprise-oriented open-weight releases. By enabling these models on the MLX backend, Ollama allows them to take advantage of the unified memory architecture and GPU acceleration found in Apple's M-series chips, which is typically more efficient on those devices than generic CPU inference.

MLX is Apple's open-source array and machine learning framework, designed specifically to exploit the unified memory of Apple Silicon so that the CPU and GPU can operate on the same data without costly copies. Ollama has been building out an MLX-based execution path alongside its long-standing reliance on llama.cpp, giving Mac users a route that is tuned for their hardware. The addition of Command A and North to the list of MLX-compatible models is consistent with this broader effort to broaden native coverage rather than treating Apple Silicon support as an afterthought.

Alongside the model news, this release updates the underlying llama.cpp engine to build 9672. The llama.cpp project is the C and C++ inference library that powers much of Ollama's cross-platform model execution, and it is updated frequently to add support for new model architectures, quantization formats, and performance optimizations. Tracking a recent build helps ensure that Ollama can load newly released models and benefit from upstream bug fixes and speed improvements. Because llama.cpp is a fast-moving dependency, keeping it close to its current state is a routine but important part of Ollama's maintenance cadence.

The release also fixes build artifacts for MLX. While the changelog does not detail the specifics, this kind of fix typically addresses problems in how compiled binaries or supporting files were packaged or distributed, which can affect whether the MLX engine installs and runs correctly for end users. Such corrections are common in point releases that follow larger feature additions, and they generally indicate that the project is stabilizing recently introduced functionality rather than changing behavior in user-facing ways.

For context, Ollama occupies a growing niche of tools that make running open-weight models locally more approachable, packaging model downloads, quantization, and a simple command line and API behind a single application. It competes and overlaps with projects such as LM Studio, llamafile, and direct use of llama.cpp, and it increasingly serves as a backend for desktop chat front ends and developer integrations. The dual-engine approach, pairing llama.cpp for broad hardware coverage with MLX for Apple-native acceleration, reflects a wider industry pattern in which inference runtimes try to match each platform's most efficient compute path.

The emphasis on Apple Silicon is notable given how widely M-series Macs are used by developers experimenting with local models. Unified memory allows these machines to load comparatively large models without dedicated discrete GPUs, and frameworks like MLX are central to extracting that capability. As more model providers release open weights, the practical question for many users is which runtime supports a given model on their specific hardware, making expanded compatibility lists a meaningful part of each release.

Users who want to take advantage of the new model support will need to update to v0.30.10 and pull the relevant Command A or North models. As with any release that bumps the llama.cpp build, it is generally advisable to verify that existing workflows and custom models continue to behave as expected. The full changelog, referenced against the prior v0.30 series, remains the authoritative source for the complete list of changes.

aded5000a6eee8b3.bodyJa:
VS CodeのGitHub Copilotでモデル選択メニューを開くと、GPTでもClaudeでもGeminiでもない見慣れない名前が並ぶようになった。「MAI-Code-1-Flash」をはじめとするMicrosoft自社開発のモデル群「MAI」だ。確認されているのは7種類で、同社が外部の基盤モデルに依存しすぎない体制づくりを進めていることを示す動きと見られる。

MAIはMicrosoft AIの略で、同社が社内で開発する大規模言語モデルのブランドである。Microsoftは2025年にテキスト生成向けの「MAI-1-preview」や音声合成の「MAI-Voice-1」を公表しており、今回のコーディング特化モデルはその系譜に連なるものと位置づけられる。「Flash」という名称からは、応答速度や軽量さを重視した構成である可能性がうかがえる。

背景には、MicrosoftとOpenAIの関係変化がある。Microsoftは長年OpenAIに巨額を出資し、CopilotやAzure OpenAI Serviceを通じてGPT系モデルを主力に据えてきた。一方で、特定の外部ベンダーへ過度に依存するリスクを避けるため、自社モデルの開発を加速させているとされる。Mustafa Suleyman氏が率いるMicrosoft AI部門が、その中核を担っていると報じられている。

Copilotはもともと複数モデルを切り替えて使える設計を採っており、利用者はOpenAIのGPT系に加え、AnthropicのClaudeやGoogleのGeminiも選べる。そこに自社のMAIが加わることで、選択肢はさらに広がる。コストの最適化や、タスクに応じた使い分けという観点でも、モデルの多様化は意味を持つ。

現時点では各MAIモデルの詳細な仕様や性能、提供範囲の全容には不明な部分も多い。GPTやClaudeといった先行モデルと比べて実務でどこまで通用するかは、今後の評価を待つ必要がある。とはいえ、Microsoftが自前のコーディングAIをCopilotの選択肢に据えた事実は、生成AI市場における基盤モデルの内製化という潮流を象徴していると言えそうだ。
aded5000a6eee8b3.bodyEn:
Developers who recently opened the model picker in GitHub Copilot inside Visual Studio Code may have noticed some unfamiliar entries among the usual choices. Alongside the established names from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google now sits a new family branded MAI, including a coding-oriented variant called MAI-Code-1-Flash. These are Microsoft's own in-house models, and their arrival in Copilot is a meaningful signal of how the company is reshaping the engine that powers its flagship developer tool.

For years, GitHub Copilot has been closely tied to OpenAI, whose GPT models drove the original code-completion experience and later the chat-based assistant. More recently, Microsoft broadened the lineup, allowing users to switch between GPT, Claude, and Gemini depending on the task at hand. The appearance of Microsoft-developed alternatives continues that diversification, but with an important difference: the company now controls more of the stack, from the underlying model to the integrated development environment that surrounds it.

According to the reporting, Microsoft is introducing seven MAI models in total, with MAI-Code-1-Flash positioned as the coding specialist. The "Flash" suffix, a convention shared with other vendors' model families, typically denotes a smaller, faster, and more cost-efficient configuration tuned for low latency rather than maximum reasoning depth. That framing fits the practical demands of coding assistance, where completions need to appear almost instantly as a developer types. A lightweight model that responds quickly can be more useful in the tight inner loop of editing than a larger model that produces marginally better answers more slowly.

The MAI branding traces back to Microsoft AI, the division led by Mustafa Suleyman, the co-founder of DeepMind and Inflection AI who joined Microsoft in 2024. That group has been steadily building first-party models, with earlier efforts reportedly including a general-purpose model and a speech-focused system. A coding-tuned MAI model is a logical extension of that strategy, and routing it into Copilot gives Microsoft a large, real-world testing ground where it can observe how its own systems perform against the strongest third-party options.

The strategic motivation appears straightforward. Relying on a single external provider for a product used by millions of developers creates both cost exposure and dependency risk. By developing competitive models internally, Microsoft can reduce inference costs, gain leverage in negotiations, and tailor behavior specifically to its tooling. It also insulates Copilot from any single partner's roadmap or pricing changes. The relationship between Microsoft and OpenAI remains deep, but the two companies' interests have grown more complex as OpenAI builds out its own products and Microsoft invests in alternatives.

For users, the immediate practical question is how MAI-Code-1-Flash compares with the incumbents on everyday tasks such as generating functions, explaining code, writing tests, and handling multi-file edits. Model quality in coding is highly task-dependent, and a model optimized for speed may trade away some capability on complex, multi-step problems. It is likely that Microsoft is positioning the Flash variant for high-frequency, latency-sensitive interactions while reserving heavier models for deeper reasoning, though the full division of labor among the seven models is not yet entirely clear from the available information.

It is worth keeping expectations measured. Benchmark numbers and marketing positioning do not always translate into a better day-to-day experience, and the value of any model in Copilot depends heavily on how it is integrated, how context is supplied, and how well it handles a given codebase. Developers can evaluate the new options directly by selecting them in the model picker and comparing results on their own work, which remains the most reliable test.

The broader context is an industry-wide move toward model choice and multi-model architectures. Rather than betting everything on one system, platform vendors increasingly offer a menu and route requests to whichever model best fits the cost, speed, and quality needs of a given moment. Microsoft adding its own models to that menu inside Copilot reflects this trend, and it suggests the company intends to compete not only as a distributor of others' AI but as a builder of its own.

467f3195299ac28d.bodyJa:
VS CodeのGitHub Copilotでモデル選択メニューを開くと、これまで見慣れなかった名前が並んでいることに気づくユーザーが増えている。その代表格が「MAI-Code-1-Flash」だ。GPTでもClaudeでもGeminiでもなく、Microsoft自身が開発したコーディング向けモデルであり、同社の自社モデル群「MAI(Microsoft AI)」がCopilotの選択肢として本格的に姿を見せ始めたことを示している。

これまでGitHub Copilotは、OpenAIのGPT系、AnthropicのClaude系、GoogleのGemini系といった外部ベンダーのモデルを切り替えて使える「マルチモデル」構成を取ってきた。ユーザーはタスクに応じて、推論力を重視するモデルと速度を重視するモデルを使い分けられる。そこにMicrosoft自身のMAIが加わった形で、複数種類のMAIモデルが利用可能になったとされる。

MAIは、Mustafa Suleyman氏が率いるMicrosoft AI部門が進める内製モデルの取り組みだ。同社は基盤モデル「MAI-1-preview」や音声モデル「MAI-Voice-1」を公開しており、今回のコーディングモデルはその延長線上に位置づけられる可能性がある。名称に含まれる「Flash」は、軽量で応答が速い領域を担うモデルであることを示唆していると見られ、コード補完やちょっとした編集など、低レイテンシが求められる用途を想定しているのかもしれない。

背景には、特定の外部ベンダーへの依存度を下げ、推論コストやレイテンシ、データの扱いを自社で最適化したいというMicrosoftの狙いがあると考えられる。OpenAIとの提携を維持しつつも、自前のモデルを育てることで、価格面の交渉力や製品設計の自由度を高められるとみられる。

利用者にとっては選択肢が増える一方で、モデルごとに得意分野や精度、対応できるコンテキスト長が異なるため、実際の開発タスクでどこまで使えるかは個別の検証が欠かせない。GPTやClaudeといった成熟した既存モデルと並べたとき、MAIがどの程度の品質を出せるのか。今後のアップデートと、現場の開発者による評価の蓄積が注目される。
467f3195299ac28d.bodyEn:
Microsoft has begun surfacing its own family of artificial intelligence models, branded MAI, inside GitHub Copilot, and developers using Visual Studio Code may now find as many as seven of them listed in the editor's model picker. The appearance of names such as MAI-Code-1-Flash—which is neither an OpenAI GPT model, an Anthropic Claude model, nor a Google Gemini model—signals that Microsoft is moving its in-house systems closer to the everyday coding workflows of millions of Copilot users.

The MAI label refers to Microsoft AI, the division the company assembled to build foundation models of its own rather than relying solely on OpenAI, its longtime partner and a company in which it holds a large investment. Microsoft introduced its first internally developed models in 2025, and the arrival of coding-oriented variants in Copilot appears to be the next step in extending that work from consumer assistants into developer tooling.

The lineup visible in the picker appears to span several distinct models rather than a single offering, suggesting Microsoft is testing different sizes and specializations at once. MAI-Code-1-Flash is the most clearly coding-focused name among them. The "Flash" suffix is notable because it echoes a convention popularized by Google's Gemini Flash line, where the word typically denotes a smaller, faster, and cheaper tier optimized for latency-sensitive tasks rather than maximum reasoning depth. A coding model tuned for speed is well suited to inline completion and chat-style assistance, where responsiveness often matters more than the deepest possible analysis. It is likely that Microsoft is positioning these models to handle high-volume, lower-cost requests while reserving heavier third-party models for more demanding work.

GitHub Copilot has gradually shifted from a single-model product into a multi-model platform. Over the past two years GitHub has added the ability to choose among models from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google directly within the Copilot interface, giving developers a menu of options that trade off cost, speed, and capability. Slotting Microsoft's own MAI models into that same picker places them in direct comparison with established competitors and lets the company route at least some traffic to infrastructure it fully controls.

The strategic logic is straightforward. Running inference for a service at the scale of Copilot is expensive, and depending on a single external provider carries both cost and supply risk. By developing models internally, Microsoft can tune them for its specific products, manage capacity on its own Azure data centers, and reduce its exposure to any one vendor. The move also fits a broader industry pattern in which large platform owners increasingly want models they own outright alongside the ones they license.

Microsoft AI is led by Mustafa Suleyman, a co-founder of DeepMind who later started Inflection AI before joining Microsoft in 2024. The group has been building both consumer-facing models and, evidently, specialized systems for tasks such as code generation. Whether the MAI coding models match the quality of the strongest GPT or Claude offerings remains to be seen, and early availability in a model picker does not necessarily mean they are intended as defaults.

For developers, the immediate practical takeaway is choice. Those who open the model selector in VS Code can experiment with the MAI options the same way they would test any other model, comparing completion quality, response speed, and behavior on their own codebases. Because results vary by programming language, project structure, and prompt style, the only reliable way to judge a new model is hands-on testing against real tasks.

The broader significance lies in what the rollout suggests about Microsoft's direction. Even as the company continues to ship products built on OpenAI's technology, it is steadily assembling an independent model stack and threading it into flagship tools. The presence of multiple MAI variants in Copilot indicates the effort is already substantial, and it is likely that the lineup will keep evolving as Microsoft refines which workloads its own models handle best. For now, the most useful response is curiosity rather than conclusions: try the models, measure them, and watch how the picker changes over the coming months.

ab36c870c3a30295.bodyJa:
画像生成AIで知られるMidjourneyが、これまでの主力事業から大きく踏み出す動きを見せている。同社CEOのDavid Holz氏は、初のハードウェア製品となるAI搭載の全身超音波スキャナーを公開し、あわせてサンフランシスコでのスパ建設計画も明らかにした。「猫の画像生成」に象徴されてきたソフトウェア企業が、医療やウェルネス領域の物理的プロダクトへと事業の幅を広げる試みとして注目される。

Midjourneyはこれまで、テキストから高品質な画像を生成するサービスを提供し、外部からの大型資金調達に頼らず独立運営を続けてきたことで知られる。今回発表された全身超音波スキャナーは、超音波による体内画像の取得にAIによる解析を組み合わせるものと見られ、同社がこれまで培ってきた画像処理や生成モデルの知見を、医療画像の分野へ応用する狙いがあると推測される。ただし、現時点で公開されている技術的な詳細は限られており、実際の精度や用途、市場投入の時期などは明らかになっていない。

医療画像の領域では、超音波画像の自動解析やノイズ除去、診断支援にAIを用いる研究や製品開発がすでに各社で進められている。スマートフォンに接続して使う携帯型超音波デバイスを手がける企業も登場しており、ハードウェアとAIを組み合わせた医療機器は一定の潮流を形成しつつある。Midjourneyの参入が、こうした既存プレイヤーとどのように差別化されるのかが今後の焦点となりそうだ。

一方で、医療機器として展開する場合には、各国の規制当局による承認や安全性・有効性の検証が不可欠となる。とりわけ米国ではFDA(食品医薬品局)の審査が大きなハードルとなり得るため、製品が一般の利用者の手に届くまでには時間を要する可能性がある。生成AIの分野で実績を持つ企業であっても、規制が厳格な医療領域では慎重なプロセスが求められる点は留意すべきだろう。

サンフランシスコでのスパ計画とあわせて見ると、今回の発表は単なる新製品の追加というより、ソフトウェア中心の事業から、身体やウェルネスに関わる体験全体へと視野を広げる姿勢の表れと受け取ることもできる。もっとも、こうした多角化が同社の本業である画像生成サービスとどのように結びつくのかは現時点では不透明であり、今後の具体的な情報公開を待つ必要がある。
ab36c870c3a30295.bodyEn:
Midjourney, the company best known for turning text prompts into striking images, says it is moving into a radically different domain: medical-grade hardware. Chief executive David Holz this week unveiled what the company describes as its first physical product, an AI-driven full-body ultrasound scanner, alongside plans to build a wellness spa in San Francisco. The announcement matters because it represents an unusually sharp pivot for a firm whose name has become shorthand for generative art, and because it places a consumer-AI darling squarely inside the heavily regulated world of medical devices.

According to Holz, the scanner is intended to capture a comprehensive internal image of the body and use machine-learning models to interpret the resulting data. Ultrasound is an appealing target for AI because the technology is non-invasive, relatively inexpensive, and uses no ionizing radiation, but it has historically required trained sonographers to operate the probe and skilled clinicians to read the images. Several companies have argued that software can lower that barrier, and Midjourney appears to be positioning its system as a way to automate both image acquisition and interpretation. The company has not yet published detailed technical specifications, clinical validation data, or regulatory timelines, so many of the most important questions about accuracy and safety remain open.

The move is less surprising in light of Holz's background. Before founding Midjourney, he co-founded Leap Motion, a company that built hand- and motion-tracking hardware, giving him direct experience shipping physical devices rather than purely software products. Midjourney itself has been notable for operating without venture capital, funding its growth through subscription revenue and remaining comparatively small. That financial independence may give it more freedom to experiment with capital-intensive projects like hardware and physical real estate than a more conventionally funded startup would have.

The accompanying plan for a San Francisco spa suggests the company is thinking about how such a device would reach people. Rather than selling a scanner directly to hospitals or shipping a consumer gadget, a spa or clinic setting would let Midjourney control the experience and gather imaging data in a supervised environment. This echoes a broader wellness and longevity trend in the technology industry, where founders and investors have poured money into preventive health, biological-age testing, and whole-body screening. Companies offering full-body MRI scans have grown popular among the health-conscious affluent, even as some physicians caution that aggressive screening of asymptomatic people can surface incidental findings that lead to unnecessary anxiety and follow-up procedures.

Midjourney is also far from alone in tying artificial intelligence to medical imaging. Handheld ultrasound makers such as Butterfly Network have spent years pairing portable probes with software guidance, and numerous startups and incumbents are building AI tools to flag abnormalities in scans. Regulators including the US Food and Drug Administration have cleared a growing number of AI-assisted imaging products, but each typically requires evidence that the system performs reliably for its intended use. Any device that claims to diagnose rather than merely assist would likely face a more demanding review. It is not yet clear where Midjourney's scanner would fall on that spectrum, or whether the company intends to pursue formal clearance.

The announcement fits a wider pattern of consumer-AI companies reaching beyond their original products into hardware. OpenAI has partnered with the designer Jony Ive on a device, while firms like Humane and Rabbit have tried, with mixed results, to build dedicated AI gadgets. Translating frontier models into dependable, physical, real-world products has proven difficult, and a medical instrument raises the stakes considerably, since errors carry health consequences rather than aesthetic ones.

For now, much about Midjourney's plan remains unproven. The company has a track record of rapid iteration in software, but building, validating, and lawfully deploying a medical scanner is a different and slower undertaking. Whether the project signals a genuine strategic shift or a more exploratory side bet should become clearer as Midjourney releases technical details, demonstrates clinical results, and clarifies how it intends to navigate medical regulation.

7ff96fa315614a27.bodyJa:
AIコードエディタ「Cursor」を提供するAnysphereは、繰り返し作業を自動化する機能「Cursor Automations」を大幅に強化した。新たに自然言語で自動化を組み立てられる「/automate」スキル、GitHubおよびSlack向けの新しいトリガー、そしてコンピューター操作（computer use）のサポートを追加し、常時稼働するエージェントによる定型業務の自動化をより実用的なものにした。

Cursor Automationsは、開発者が手作業で繰り返していたタスクを、バックグラウンドで動き続けるエージェントに肩代わりさせる仕組みである。今回のアップデートの目玉である「/automate」スキルは、エディタ内のチャットから自然言語で指示するだけで自動化を設定できるとされ、専用の設定画面を細かく操作する手間を減らす狙いがあると見られる。

新しいトリガーの追加により、自動化の起点が広がった点も重要だ。GitHub連携では、プルリクエストの作成やイシューの更新といったリポジトリ上のイベントを契機にエージェントを起動できるようになると見られる。Slack連携では、特定のメッセージやコマンドをきっかけに処理を走らせる運用が想定され、チーム内のコミュニケーションと開発フローを橋渡しする使い方が見込まれる。

さらに注目されるのが、コンピューター操作のサポートである。これはエージェントがブラウザやアプリケーションの画面を認識し、人間のようにクリックや入力を行ってタスクを進める技術を指す。Anthropicの「Computer Use」やOpenAIの「Operator」など、近年は大手AIベンダーが同種の機能を相次いで投入しており、コード生成にとどまらず実際の操作まで自動化する流れが広がりつつある。

背景には、AIエージェントを単発の補助ツールから、継続的に業務を回す「自律的な働き手」へと位置づけ直す業界全体の動きがある。GitHub CopilotやDevinといった競合も自律エージェント路線を強めており、Cursorの今回の強化はその潮流に沿ったものといえる。一方で、常時稼働するエージェントに外部サービスの操作権限を与える際は、誤動作や情報漏えいといったリスクの管理が前提となる点には留意が必要だろう。導入にあたっては、対象範囲や権限を絞り込みながら段階的に活用していくことが現実的と考えられる。
7ff96fa315614a27.bodyEn:
Cursor has expanded its Automations feature, adding a new way to create automated workflows, fresh triggers for GitHub and Slack, and support for computer use. The update matters because it pushes Cursor further beyond an interactive coding assistant toward a platform where always-on agents handle recurring engineering tasks without a developer initiating each run. For teams already using Cursor day to day, this lowers the barrier to offloading routine maintenance, triage, and review work to background processes.

At the center of the release is the new /automate skill. Rather than configuring an automation through settings or scripts, developers can describe what they want in natural language and let Cursor assemble the corresponding workflow. This mirrors a broader pattern in the company's product design, where capabilities are increasingly exposed as conversational skills that the agent can invoke. The approach appears intended to reduce setup friction, letting users go from an idea, such as "summarize new pull requests every morning," to a working automation with minimal manual configuration.

The new triggers are arguably the most consequential part of the update because they determine when automations fire. With GitHub integration, automations can respond to repository events, which in practice could mean reacting to new pull requests, issues, comments, or pushes. This positions Cursor to participate in workflows that have traditionally been handled by continuous integration systems or bots like Dependabot and GitHub Actions. The Slack integration extends the same idea into team communication, allowing automations to be triggered from messages or channels so that an agent can act on a request raised in conversation. Together, these triggers connect Cursor's agents to the two surfaces where much engineering coordination already happens.

Support for computer use is the most technically ambitious addition. Computer use generally refers to an agent's ability to operate a graphical interface directly, controlling a virtual screen, mouse, and keyboard rather than relying solely on code or API calls. The concept gained prominence after Anthropic introduced a computer use capability for its Claude models, and it has since become a focus across the industry as vendors explore agents that can navigate applications a human would normally click through. Within Cursor Automations, this likely enables agents to complete tasks that have no clean programmatic interface, such as interacting with web dashboards or legacy tools, though the practical reliability of such interactions tends to vary and is worth testing case by case.

To understand why these additions fit together, it helps to recall what Cursor is. It is an AI-centric code editor, originally built as a fork of Visual Studio Code, that integrates large language models for code completion, chat, and agentic editing across a codebase. Its Agent functionality can plan and execute multi-step changes, and Automations build on that foundation by letting those agents run on a schedule or in response to events rather than only when a developer is actively typing. The always-on framing is key: the value proposition is that repetitive work continues even when no one is at the keyboard.

This release also sits within a competitive landscape where several tools are converging on similar ideas. GitHub's own Copilot has moved toward agent-style features and autonomous pull request handling, while assistants such as Claude Code, OpenAI's Codex tooling, and Devin-style autonomous agents all pursue background or long-running task execution. By tying its automations to GitHub and Slack and layering in computer use, Cursor appears to be aligning with this direction, aiming to keep developers within its environment for both interactive and unattended work.

For teams considering adoption, a few practical points are worth keeping in mind. Granting agents the ability to act on repository events or operate interfaces raises the usual questions about permissions, scope, and review, so it is prudent to constrain what automations can touch and to monitor their output. As with any agent-driven system, results can be inconsistent, and human oversight remains advisable for anything that merges code or affects production. The changelog presents these features as enhancements rather than a finished product, and their real-world usefulness will likely become clearer as users apply them to concrete, repetitive workflows.

5ea30ecf68e27c27.bodyJa:
中国のAI企業Z.aiが、大規模言語モデルの最新版「GLM-5.2」をオープンウェイトとして公開した。テキスト専用モデルとしては現時点で最高水準の性能を備えるとされ、誰でも自由に利用・改変できるMITライセンスで提供される点が注目を集めている。

Z.aiは2026年6月13日にまずコーディング支援プランの契約者向けにGLM-5.2を提供し、続く6月16日にモデルの重み(ウェイト)一式をMITライセンスで一般公開した。MITライセンスは商用利用や再配布、改変に対する制約が極めて緩い寛容なライセンスであり、企業や研究者が自社製品に組み込んだり、ファインチューニングを施したりする際のハードルが低い。オープンウェイトのLLMでは利用条件に独自の制限を設ける例も少なくないため、この選択は開発者コミュニティにとって歓迎されやすい。

モデルのサイズは前世代とほぼ同程度に抑えられているとされる。パラメータ数を大きく増やさずに性能を高めている場合、学習データや手法の改良が寄与した可能性がある。同規模のまま品質を引き上げられれば、推論に必要な計算資源やメモリの面でも扱いやすく、ローカル環境での実行を志向するユーザーにとって利点となる。

ここで重要なのは「テキスト専用」という限定だ。GLM-5.2は画像や音声を扱うマルチモーダル機能を主眼としておらず、あくまで文章生成や推論、コーディングといったテキスト中心のタスクで強みを発揮すると位置づけられている。マルチモーダル対応モデルとは評価軸が異なるため、単純な優劣比較には注意が必要だ。

近年、中国発のオープンウェイトモデルは存在感を増しており、DeepSeekやAlibabaのQwen、Moonshot AIのKimiなどが相次いで高性能モデルを公開してきた。GLMシリーズもその系譜に連なり、今回の公開は欧米のクローズドな商用モデルに対するオープン陣営の追い上げを象徴する動きと見られる。実際の性能評価はコミュニティによる検証を経て定まっていくとみられるが、寛容なライセンスと比較的小さなサイズの組み合わせは、幅広い採用を後押しする可能性がある。
5ea30ecf68e27c27.bodyEn:
Chinese AI lab Z.ai has released GLM-5.2, and early indications suggest it may be the strongest text-only open-weights large language model available today. The model was first made available to subscribers of the lab's coding plan on June 13th, before the full weights were published under a permissive MIT license on June 16th. For developers and organisations that want capable models they can download, run, and modify themselves, the release is a notable data point in an increasingly competitive open-weights landscape.

The headline claim is that GLM-5.2 sits at the top of the text-only category, meaning models that handle text input and output without native image, audio, or video understanding. That framing matters, because some of the most capable open-weights systems are multimodal, and comparing across those categories can be misleading. Within its own lane, GLM-5.2 appears to perform at or near the frontier, though as always with new releases, independent benchmark verification and real-world testing will be needed before such claims can be treated as settled.

GLM-5.2 is reportedly similar in size to its predecessor, which is significant for anyone planning to deploy it. Keeping the parameter count roughly stable while improving performance suggests gains came from training data, architecture refinements, or post-training techniques rather than simply scaling up. For local users, a stable size means the hardware requirements and quantisation strategies that worked for the earlier model should carry over, lowering the friction of upgrading. Larger open-weights models typically still demand substantial GPU memory, and many people rely on quantised versions, formats such as GGUF, and tools like llama.cpp, Ollama, or vLLM to run them on more modest setups.

The choice of an MIT license is worth highlighting. MIT is one of the most permissive licenses in common use, placing few restrictions on commercial use, modification, or redistribution. This contrasts with the custom community licenses that some other model providers attach to their weights, which can include usage caps, acceptable-use clauses, or restrictions on training competing models. By opting for MIT, Z.ai is signalling an intent to maximise adoption, including in commercial products, which can be a meaningful advantage for companies wary of ambiguous licensing terms.

It is worth being precise about terminology here. Open weights is not the same as open source. Releasing the weights lets others run and fine-tune the model, but it does not necessarily include the training data, the full training code, or detailed documentation of the process. GLM-5.2 should be understood as an open-weights release under an open-source-style license for the artefact itself, rather than a fully reproducible open-source project. That distinction affects how much downstream users can audit or recreate the model from scratch.

The release also fits a broader pattern. Over the past couple of years, Chinese labs have become central to the open-weights ecosystem, with the GLM series from Z.ai sitting alongside work from groups such as DeepSeek, Alibaba's Qwen line, and Moonshot's Kimi models. These organisations have repeatedly shipped competitive weights under relatively permissive terms, putting pressure on Western labs that have often kept their strongest systems behind APIs. The result is a fast-moving field where the definition of "best open model" can shift within weeks, and where the gap between proprietary frontier models and the best open alternatives appears to be narrowing, at least on many published benchmarks.

For practitioners, the practical takeaways are straightforward. If GLM-5.2 lives up to the early assessment, it becomes a strong candidate for self-hosted deployments, coding assistants, and applications where data privacy, cost control, or offline operation rule out cloud APIs. The text-only focus means it is not the right tool for tasks requiring image or audio understanding, where dedicated multimodal models remain necessary. As with any new model, prospective users should run their own evaluations on representative tasks, since leaderboard performance does not always translate to specific workloads. Independent testing in the days following the release will likely clarify exactly where GLM-5.2 stands relative to both open and closed competitors.

250921170ee23bab.bodyJa:
クラウドの生成AIサービスが突然使えなくなったときに備え、手元のPCだけで最低限の作業をこなせる環境を持っておきたい。そんな動機からローカルLLMで長文要約に挑んだ筆者が、処理に「とてつもなく時間がかかった」体験を共有している。記事は失敗談の体裁を取りつつ、ローカル環境で大規模言語モデルを扱う際の現実的な制約を浮き彫りにしている。

筆者は以前、Ubuntu上で軽量モデルのGemma系（E2B）を動かす記事を執筆しており、その延長として長文の要約に取り組んだという。狙いはシンプルで、外部APIに依存せず手元で文章を処理できる安心感を確保することだった。生成AIは便利な一方、障害や仕様変更、料金体系の改定などで急に使えなくなる可能性があり、ローカルで動く代替手段への関心は近年高まっている。

しかし実際に試すと、要約が完了するまでに想定をはるかに超える時間を要した。筆者自身は「自分の環境とやり方がイケてなかった話」と振り返っており、原因をモデルやツールだけに帰さず、設定や手順の問題として整理している点が特徴だ。

長文の処理が重くなる背景には、いくつかの一般的な要因が考えられる。LLMは入力された文章をトークン単位で読み込み、文脈として保持しながら出力を生成する。入力が長いほど読み込み（プレフィル）の計算量が増え、扱えるコンテキスト長を超える場合は分割処理が必要になる。GPUのVRAMやメモリが十分でない環境では、CPU処理へのフォールバックや量子化モデルの選択が速度に大きく影響する可能性がある。

こうした課題に対しては、llama.cppやOllamaといった推論ツールでの設定見直し、より小さな量子化モデルの採用、文章を分割して段階的に要約する手法などが一般に知られている。クラウド側でもOpenAIやAnthropic、Googleなどが長文対応を競うが、ローカルでは限られたハードウェア資源とどう折り合いをつけるかが鍵になる。

今回の記事は華々しい成功例ではないものの、ローカルLLMを実運用に近づけるうえで踏むべき試行錯誤を具体的に示している。同様の環境構築を検討する読者にとって、つまずきやすい点を事前に知る手がかりとなりそうだ。
250921170ee23bab.bodyEn:
Running large language models locally has become increasingly practical, but a recent experiment in summarizing long documents on a personal Ubuntu machine highlights a persistent gap between cloud and local inference: speed. The author had previously written about running a compact Gemma model, referred to as Gemma 4 E2B, on Ubuntu, motivated by a desire to keep a minimal local fallback in case cloud generative AI services suddenly become unavailable. When that same setup was pointed at a long-form summarization task, however, the process took dramatically longer than expected.

The core lesson, as the author candidly notes, is that the slowdown stemmed largely from the environment and the chosen approach rather than from a fundamental flaw in local LLMs. That distinction matters, because it suggests the bottleneck is something a user can address through configuration rather than an inherent limit of running models on modest hardware.

Long-context tasks stress local inference in ways that short prompts do not. To summarize a long document, a model must first read and encode the entire input, a phase often called prompt processing or prefill, before it can begin generating output tokens. The prefill cost scales with the number of input tokens, and on hardware without a capable GPU, or with limited memory bandwidth, this initial pass alone can consume substantial time. A short chat prompt may feel instantaneous, while a document of several thousand tokens forces the model to grind through a far larger computation before producing a single word.

Several factors compound the problem. Small, quantized models such as the E2B variant are designed to fit modest memory budgets, but quantization and CPU-bound execution can reduce throughput, typically measured in tokens per second. If inference runs primarily on the CPU rather than a GPU, both prefill and decoding slow considerably. The context window matters too: feeding an entire long article in one pass maximizes prefill work, and if the input approaches or exceeds the model's effective context length, quality may degrade even as processing time grows.

It helps to understand the surrounding tooling. Many enthusiasts run local models through frameworks such as Ollama, llama.cpp, or LM Studio, which wrap the underlying inference engines and handle model downloads and quantization formats like GGUF. These tools make setup approachable but also expose users to configuration choices, including thread counts, GPU offload layers, and batch sizes, that strongly affect performance. For heavier workloads, projects such as vLLM aim for higher throughput through techniques like paged attention, though they generally assume server-class GPUs.

There are practical mitigations. A common pattern is to split the document into smaller segments, summarize each piece, and then combine the results, an approach sometimes described as map-reduce summarization. Reducing input length, choosing a more aggressively optimized quantization, enabling GPU offload where available, or selecting a model sized appropriately for the hardware can all help. The trade-off is that smaller models and aggressive chunking risk losing nuance, so there is a balance to strike between speed and summary quality.

The broader motivation is worth noting. The author's underlying goal, maintaining a local capability that does not depend on cloud availability, reflects a wider interest in resilience and privacy. Local models keep data on-device and remain usable during outages or in restricted network environments. The Gemma family from Google, alongside open-weight models such as Meta's Llama, Mistral's releases, and Alibaba's Qwen, has made this kind of self-hosting increasingly viable, with compact variants aimed specifically at laptops and modest desktops.

The takeaway is measured. Local LLMs can summarize long texts, but doing so quickly requires matching the model, quantization, and inference settings to the hardware, and structuring the task to limit prefill cost. The experience appears to be less a verdict on local inference as a whole and more a reminder that performance is highly sensitive to configuration. For anyone building a personal offline fallback, benchmarking token throughput and experimenting with chunking before relying on the setup in a pinch is likely time well spent.

8d34e31f4773f3fc.bodyJa:
A2A（Agent-to-Agent）プロトコルが公開から1周年を迎えた。Googleは記念ブログで、異なるベンダーやフレームワークで作られた自律型AIエージェントが、互いに安全に連携してタスクを引き渡せるオープンな枠組みの到達点と今後の方向性を示した。単体で動くエージェントから、複数のエージェントが役割分担しながら協働する「マルチエージェント」へと、開発の重心が移りつつあることを象徴する節目といえる。

A2Aは、エージェント同士が能力を発見し、対話し、作業を委譲するための共通言語を定義する。各エージェントは自らの機能や対応タスクを記述した「エージェントカード」を公開し、相手はそれを参照して適切な依頼先を選ぶ。やり取りはタスクやメッセージという単位で構造化され、長時間かかる処理の進捗共有や、人間による承認を挟む運用にも対応する設計とされる。内部実装を互いに公開せずに連携できる点が、企業利用での導入障壁を下げると見られている。

背景には、生成AIの利用が単発の質問応答から、複数の手順を自動でこなす「エージェント」へと拡大してきた事情がある。Anthropicが提唱したMCP（Model Context Protocol）がエージェントと外部のツールやデータを結ぶ役割を担うのに対し、A2Aはエージェント同士の水平的な連携を担うと位置づけられ、両者は競合ではなく補完関係にあると説明されることが多い。

エコシステムの広がりも進んだ。A2Aの仕様はLinux Foundation傘下のプロジェクトへ移管され、特定企業に依存しない中立的な運営を目指す体制が整えられた。公開当初からSalesforceやSAP、ServiceNowなど多数の企業が関心を示しており、対応するSDKや実装が複数の言語で整備されつつある。

一方で、標準化の取り組みは緒に就いたばかりで、相互運用性の検証やセキュリティ、認証・権限管理といった実運用上の課題はなお残る。複数ベンダーのエージェントが入り乱れる環境では、信頼性や責任の所在をどう担保するかも論点となりそうだ。A2Aがその共通基盤として定着するかは、今後の採用状況とコミュニティの成熟度に左右される可能性がある。
8d34e31f4773f3fc.bodyEn:
The Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol has reached its first anniversary, a milestone that the Google Developers blog uses to take stock of how far the open standard has come and where it may head next. A2A matters because it addresses a problem that has grown more urgent as autonomous AI agents proliferate: how agents built by different teams, on different frameworks, and hosted by different vendors can discover one another, communicate, and safely hand off work without brittle, point-to-point integrations.

At its core, A2A is an open protocol that lets independent agents collaborate while remaining opaque to one another. Rather than requiring each agent to expose its internal logic, memory, or proprietary tooling, A2A defines a common language for them to negotiate and exchange tasks over standard web technologies such as HTTP, JSON-RPC, and server-sent events. This design means an agent can act as a client requesting help from another agent acting as a remote service, without either side needing to share how it works internally.

A central concept is the Agent Card, a machine-readable document, typically published as JSON, that advertises an agent's identity, capabilities, endpoint, and authentication requirements. Other agents can read this card to decide whether a given agent is suited to a task before initiating contact. Once a connection is established, work is organized around tasks that move through a defined lifecycle, from submission through working states to completion or failure. The protocol also supports long-running jobs and streaming updates, so an agent handling a complex request can report incremental progress rather than forcing the requester to wait for a single final response.

Security and identity are recurring themes in A2A's design, reflecting the risks inherent in letting software agents act on a user's behalf. The protocol leans on established enterprise authentication patterns and is intended to operate within existing identity and access frameworks rather than inventing new ones. This emphasis appears aimed at making the standard palatable to organizations that are cautious about granting autonomy to AI systems.

A2A is frequently described alongside the Model Context Protocol (MCP), an open standard popularized by Anthropic. The two are best understood as complementary rather than competing. MCP focuses on connecting a single agent to tools, data sources, and context, effectively giving one agent the resources it needs. A2A focuses on the layer above that, connecting agents to other agents so they can delegate and coordinate. A practical system might use MCP to equip an agent with capabilities and A2A to let that agent collaborate with peers.

When A2A was first introduced, Google presented it with support from a broad roster of technology and consulting partners, signaling an intent to build an industry-wide standard rather than a proprietary one. The project was subsequently placed under open governance, with stewardship moving to the Linux Foundation, a step that is likely intended to reassure adopters that no single company controls the protocol's direction. Google has also tied A2A into its own developer tooling, including the Agent Development Kit (ADK) and the Vertex AI platform, while stressing that the protocol itself is framework-agnostic and meant to work with agents built elsewhere.

The broader context is an industry moving rapidly toward multi-agent systems, in which specialized agents handle discrete parts of a workflow and pass results between them. Proponents argue that such architectures can be more modular, scalable, and maintainable than monolithic agents that try to do everything at once. Skeptics note that coordination, error handling, and accountability become harder as the number of autonomous participants grows, which is part of why a shared protocol with clear task semantics and authentication is seen as valuable.

Whether A2A becomes the default connective tissue for these systems will depend on continued adoption, interoperability testing across vendors, and how well it coexists with adjacent standards. For now, the anniversary post positions A2A as a maturing foundation, with expanding tooling and a governance model designed for longevity, while acknowledging that the agent ecosystem remains early and fast-moving. Developers evaluating the protocol are likely to weigh it less as a finished product than as an evolving standard whose value grows with the size of the network that supports it.

06adf21a771cab75.bodyJa:
数千に及ぶ機密ネットワークへのアクセスを可能にする認証情報が大規模な侵害によって流出したことが明らかになった。被害組織にはOracle、Lenovo、FedEx、NATOの請負業者、そしてセキュリティ機器大手のFortinetといった重要な企業・機関が含まれるとされ、影響範囲の広さから関係者の間で警戒が高まっている。

報じられている内容によれば、今回流出したのは単なるパスワードの羅列にとどまらず、企業の内部ネットワークやシステムへ直接ログインできる有効な資格情報を多数含むとみられる。こうした認証情報が攻撃者の手に渡れば、フィッシングや脆弱性の悪用といった初期侵入の段階を経ずに、いきなり標的の環境へ侵入できる恐れがある。とりわけNATOの請負業者やセキュリティ製品を手がけるFortinetのような組織が含まれる点は、機微性の高い情報や広範な顧客基盤に波及するリスクをはらんでいる。

近年、この種の認証情報漏えいは、利用者の端末から保存済みのログイン情報やセッション情報を盗み出す「インフォスティーラー」と呼ばれるマルウェアによって引き起こされる事例が増えている。盗まれたデータは地下フォーラムやテレグラムのチャンネルなどで売買され、いわゆる「初期アクセスブローカー」がランサムウェア攻撃者などに転売する流通構造が指摘されてきた。今回の侵害がどの経路で発生したかは現時点で確定的ではないものの、こうした既存の脅威の延長線上にある可能性がある。

認証情報の流出が深刻なのは、二次被害が連鎖しやすい点にある。漏れた資格情報を起点にサプライチェーン全体へ攻撃が広がったり、多要素認証(MFA)が未設定のアカウントが乗っ取られたりする懸念がある。専門家は一般に、こうした事態への対策として、影響を受けた可能性のあるアカウントのパスワード即時変更、MFAの導入、不審なアクセスログの監視、そして端末上のマルウェア感染の有無の確認を推奨している。

被害組織からの公式な説明や流出規模の正確な検証は今後進むとみられ、利用者や取引先は続報に注意を払う必要がある。大手企業が名を連ねる今回の事案は、サプライチェーン全体で認証情報をどう保護するかという課題を改めて突きつけたといえる。
06adf21a771cab75.bodyEn:
A newly disclosed breach has exposed working credentials for thousands of sensitive corporate and government networks, with reported victims including Oracle, Lenovo, FedEx, a contractor tied to NATO, and the security vendor Fortinet. The scale of the exposure matters because stolen credentials are among the most direct routes attackers use to slip past perimeter defenses, often bypassing the firewalls, intrusion detection, and other controls that organizations invest heavily to maintain.

According to the reporting, the leaked data consists of usernames, passwords, and in many cases the specific URLs or systems they unlock, ranging from email and VPN portals to internal administrative consoles and cloud management dashboards. Credentials of this type are especially valuable to intruders because they allow access that looks legitimate. When an attacker logs in with a valid account rather than exploiting a software flaw, the activity can blend into normal traffic and evade detection for extended periods. The presence of a NATO-linked contractor and a security firm such as Fortinet among the affected parties underscores that no sector, including defense and cybersecurity itself, is immune.

The data appears to have been collected by so-called infostealer malware, a category of credential-harvesting software that has grown into one of the most significant threats of recent years. Infostealers such as Lumma, RedLine, Raccoon, and Vidar typically infect individual machines through phishing emails, malicious advertisements, pirated software, or fake browser updates. Once installed, they scrape saved passwords from browsers, session cookies, cryptocurrency wallet data, and authentication tokens, then transmit the harvested information to servers controlled by the operators. The stolen records are frequently packaged into large collections, often called logs, and sold or traded on underground forums and Telegram channels. Aggregations of this kind can swell to billions of individual entries as logs from many separate infections are merged.

This incident fits a broader pattern in which compromised credentials, rather than novel exploits, drive a large share of intrusions. Industry analyses, including the annual Verizon Data Breach Investigations Report, have repeatedly identified stolen credentials and phishing as leading factors in breaches. High-profile attacks attributed to groups such as Scattered Spider and the operators behind various ransomware campaigns have frequently begun with valid logins purchased from initial access brokers, intermediaries who specialize in obtaining and reselling network footholds. A single exposed VPN or remote-access account can serve as the entry point for data theft, extortion, or the deployment of ransomware across an entire organization.

The appearance of credentials linked to major technology and infrastructure providers is particularly concerning because of the potential for downstream effects. A foothold inside a vendor that supplies software, hardware, or services to thousands of customers can become a stepping stone to those customers, a dynamic seen in earlier supply-chain incidents. It is important to note, however, that the presence of an organization's credentials in such a dataset does not by itself confirm that the organization's core systems were breached. Many leaked logins originate from employee or contractor devices infected outside corporate control, or from third-party services, and some entries may be outdated or already invalidated.

For affected organizations, the standard response is to assume exposed credentials are compromised and to rotate them immediately, revoke active sessions, and inspect logs for unauthorized access. Security professionals broadly recommend multifactor authentication as a critical mitigation, since a stolen password alone is far less useful when a second verification factor is required, though attackers have increasingly turned to session-cookie theft and real-time phishing to defeat some forms of it. Additional measures include adopting phishing-resistant authentication such as hardware security keys or passkeys, monitoring for anomalous login behavior, and deploying endpoint protection capable of detecting infostealer activity.

The broader lesson reinforced by this disclosure is that credential hygiene now functions as a frontline defense. Services such as Have I Been Pwned and various commercial threat-intelligence platforms track exposed credentials to help organizations and individuals identify when their accounts surface in leaked collections. As infostealer operations continue to industrialize and the market for stolen access matures, breaches assembled from harvested logins are likely to remain a persistent feature of the threat landscape, placing a premium on rapid detection, strong authentication, and the assumption that any single password may already be in adversary hands.

e78cf954e64f0310.bodyJa:
ローカルでの大規模言語モデル（LLM）実行を手軽にするツール「Ollama」が、バージョン0.30.10のリリース候補版（rc1）を公開した。今回の更新は機能追加よりも開発基盤の安定化に重点を置いたもので、macOS向けビルドの再現性を高める内容が中心となっている。

公開されたリリースノートによると、主な変更点はmacOS（Darwin）向けの継続的インテグレーション（CI）パイプラインにおいて、ビルドに用いるXcodeのバージョンを固定した点だ（PR #16788）。CIはコードの変更を自動的に検証・ビルドする仕組みで、ここで使われるツールチェーンのバージョンが予期せず変動すると、生成されるバイナリの挙動が変わったり、ビルドが失敗したりする可能性がある。Xcodeを特定の版に固定することで、こうしたばらつきを抑え、配布物の品質を一定に保つ狙いがあると見られる。

リリース候補版は正式リリース前にバグや互換性の問題を洗い出すための段階で、一般利用者よりも開発者や早期検証を行うユーザーに向けた位置づけだ。今回のように内部のビルド工程に関する修正が中心の場合、エンドユーザーが日常的に体感する変化は小さいものの、安定したバイナリ供給はプロジェクト全体の信頼性に直結する。

Ollamaはllama.cppを基盤とし、コマンド一つで多様なオープンモデルをダウンロードして実行できる点が支持を集めている。近年はLM StudioやJanといった同種のローカルLLM実行環境も登場し、プライバシー保護やオフライン利用、コスト管理の観点から、クラウドAPIに依存しない選択肢への関心が高まっている。こうした競争環境のなかで、頻繁なリリースと地道な基盤改善を続ける姿勢は、Ollamaの開発体制が成熟しつつあることを示していると言えそうだ。

正式版での追加変更の有無は今後のリリースノートで確認する必要があるが、macOSユーザーにとっては、より安定したビルドが提供される下地が整えられた格好だ。
e78cf954e64f0310.bodyEn:
Ollama has published v0.30.10-rc1, a release candidate for its widely used local large language model runtime. Release candidates like this one are not intended for everyday production use; instead, they give maintainers, packagers, and early adopters a chance to validate changes before they are promoted to a stable build. For a project that many developers rely on to run open models on their own hardware, even small infrastructure changes are worth tracking because they can affect download integrity, platform support, and the reliability of future releases.

According to the release notes, the single highlighted change in this candidate is a continuous integration adjustment: pinning the Xcode version used for the Darwin (macOS) release pipeline, tracked as pull request #16788. The stated goal is to ensure the stability of macOS builds. While this is a behind-the-scenes change rather than a new user-facing feature, it speaks directly to the consistency of the binaries that macOS users ultimately install.

To understand why this matters, it helps to know what "pinning" means in a build context. Continuous integration systems compile and package software automatically on hosted runners. Those runners are periodically updated by the provider, and on macOS the available Xcode toolchain, which includes the Apple compilers, SDKs, and code-signing utilities, can shift when the underlying image is upgraded. If a project always uses whatever Xcode version happens to be default, an unannounced toolchain bump can change compiler behavior, alter linked system libraries, or break the build outright. Pinning to a specific Xcode version removes that variability, making the Darwin build reproducible and insulating it from surprises in the CI environment. This is a common maintenance practice across many native software projects, not unique to Ollama.

For Ollama specifically, macOS is a particularly important target. The project is closely associated with running models efficiently on Apple Silicon, where Metal-based GPU acceleration allows consumer Macs to perform inference that would otherwise require dedicated hardware. Because that acceleration depends on Apple's frameworks and the toolchain used to compile against them, the macOS build path is sensitive to exactly which Xcode and SDK versions are present. A pinned configuration reduces the risk that a routine CI update could degrade performance or compatibility on those machines.

Some background on the project rounds out the picture. Ollama is an open tool that packages model runtimes, weights, and a simple command-line and API interface so users can pull and run open models locally with minimal setup. It builds on the broader ecosystem around llama.cpp and the GGUF model format, and it supports a range of open-weight model families that users can download through its registry. It runs across macOS, Linux, and Windows, and exposes a local HTTP API that has made it a common backend for desktop chat front-ends, coding assistants, and developer experimentation where data privacy, offline operation, or cost control are priorities.

The decision to surface a CI fix as the basis for a release candidate is consistent with how the project iterates. Ollama tends to ship frequently, with point releases that bundle model support, bug fixes, and infrastructure improvements. Routing such a change through an rc1 build, rather than directly into a stable tag, appears to reflect a cautious approach: the maintainers can confirm that the pinned toolchain produces working, correctly signed macOS artifacts before a wider rollout. If no regressions surface during the candidate phase, a corresponding stable v0.30.10 release would typically follow.

For most end users, the practical takeaway is modest. There is no indication of new model capabilities, API changes, or performance features in this particular candidate, so there is little reason for general users to switch from a current stable build solely on the basis of these notes. The change is most relevant to those who care about build provenance and platform reliability, including downstream packagers and contributors. Anyone evaluating the rc1 build should treat it as a pre-release and verify it against their own workflows. As always, readers seeking the authoritative list of changes should consult the project's official release page and the linked pull request, since release-candidate contents can be revised before the final version is published.

647c380836a38387.bodyJa:
Nvidiaが、ロボットのAIに自己改善を促すプログラムを示し、複数のAIコーディングエージェントが連携してロボットの訓練を自律的に指示する仕組みを公開した。GPUの取り付けやジップタイ（結束バンド）の切断といった、これまで人手による細かな調整が必要だった物理作業をロボットに習得させたという。

従来、ロボットに新しい動作を覚えさせる際には、エンジニアが報酬関数を設計し、シミュレーション環境のパラメータを調整しながら、失敗を繰り返して訓練コードを書き換える必要があった。この作業は専門知識を要し時間もかかるため、ロボットが扱えるタスクを増やすうえでのボトルネックとなってきた。

今回の取り組みでは、大規模言語モデルを基盤とする複数のAIエージェントが役割を分担し、訓練に必要なコードや報酬関数を自ら生成・修正すると見られる。シミュレーション上で大量の試行を回して結果を評価し、次の改善につなげることで、人間の介在を抑えながら性能を高めていく流れだ。

背景には、同社が展開するロボット開発基盤の存在がある。物理シミュレーターのIsaac SimやIsaac Lab、人型ロボット向けの基盤モデルGR00T、エッジ向け演算ハードウェアのJetsonなどを組み合わせ、仮想空間で学んだ動作を実機に移す「sim-to-real」と呼ばれる手法が鍵となる。

ロボティクス分野では、Google DeepMindのRT-2やTesla Optimus、Figure AIなどが汎用的な作業をこなすロボットの開発を競っており、AIエージェントに訓練そのものを任せる発想はその延長線上にあると言える。細かな物理作業を自律的に習得できれば、製造や物流の現場で応用が広がる可能性がある。

一方で、自己改善のループがどこまで安定して機能するか、現実世界での安全性や再現性をどう検証するかは引き続き課題となりそうだ。AIがAIを訓練する仕組みは効率化の余地が大きい半面、想定外の挙動を生むリスクも指摘されており、実用化に向けては慎重な評価が求められると見られる。
647c380836a38387.bodyEn:
Nvidia has detailed an experimental program in which teams of AI coding agents autonomously direct the training of robots, reportedly teaching them to perform fiddly physical tasks such as installing a GPU into a server and cutting zip ties. The effort matters because it points toward a future in which the slow, expert-driven work of programming robot behaviors could be partly handed off to software that writes, tests, and refines its own training routines, potentially compressing development cycles that currently take human engineers weeks or months.

At the center of the approach is the idea of a self-improvement loop. Rather than having human researchers hand-tune the reward functions, motion policies, and training curricula that teach a robot a new skill, the system enlists multiple large language model agents to handle those tasks. These agents appear to operate much like the AI coding assistants now common in software development, generating code, evaluating the outcomes, and iterating on their own work. In a robotics context, that means proposing how a task should be broken down, writing the logic that scores success or failure, and adjusting parameters when a behavior does not converge.

The two demonstrated tasks are notable for being grounded in real manual labor rather than abstract benchmarks. Installing a GPU requires aligning a card with a slot, applying controlled force, and seating connectors precisely, while cutting zip ties demands locating a thin target and manipulating a tool with care. Both involve contact-rich manipulation, the category of problems that has long frustrated roboticists because small errors in force or position can cause failures that are hard to model. Teaching robots to handle such tasks reliably has typically required extensive human demonstration or painstaking manual engineering.

The work fits within Nvidia's broader push into what it calls physical AI. The company has built an extended stack of robotics tools, including the Isaac platform for robot development, the Omniverse simulation environment, and the GR00T family of foundation models aimed at humanoid and general-purpose robots. A recurring theme across these tools is heavy reliance on simulation. By training robots in virtual environments, developers can run enormous numbers of trials in parallel and far faster than real time, then attempt to transfer the learned behavior to physical hardware, a process commonly referred to as sim-to-real transfer. The coding agents in this program likely lean on that simulation infrastructure to test the policies they generate before any robot touches a real component.

The use of AI agents to orchestrate training reflects a wider industry trend. Over the past two years, so-called agentic AI systems, which chain together reasoning, tool use, and iterative self-correction, have moved from research demonstrations into commercial coding assistants and automated workflows. Applying that same pattern to robotics is a logical, if ambitious, extension. The premise is that reward design and curriculum tuning, traditionally seen as a craft requiring specialized intuition, can be framed as an optimization problem that agents are well suited to explore. Earlier academic work, including Nvidia-affiliated research on automated reward generation, suggested that language models can sometimes produce reward functions that match or exceed human-designed ones.

Several caveats are worth keeping in mind. Carefully staged demonstrations do not necessarily indicate broad reliability, and contact-rich tasks that succeed in controlled conditions can degrade when lighting, object placement, or hardware varies. The gap between simulation and the physical world remains a persistent challenge, and the degree of human oversight involved in the demonstrated results is not always clear from promotional material. It also remains to be seen how well the approach generalizes beyond the specific tasks shown, or how much computing cost the iterative agent-driven training requires.

Still, the direction is significant for the robotics field, which has been searching for ways to scale skill acquisition without scaling the number of human experts proportionally. If agents can dependably author and refine their own training pipelines, the bottleneck shifts from human labor toward compute and simulation fidelity, areas where Nvidia has a clear commercial interest as a supplier of both chips and software. The demonstrations should be read as early-stage research rather than a finished product, but they illustrate how the convergence of agentic AI and robotics is beginning to reshape how machines are taught to act in the physical world.

a3d032e5da368cd8.bodyJa:
AIを悪用したサイバー攻撃が急速に高度化・大量化するなか、Microsoftの公式ブログ「Source」が、同社のIDおよびアクセス管理基盤Microsoft Entraに関連する解説として、組織や個人が最新の脅威に先手を打つための防御戦略をまとめた。攻撃側がAIを取り入れることで脅威の質と量が変化しているという認識は、業界全体で共有されつつある。

背景にあるのは、生成AIによって攻撃の準備コストが大きく下がっている点だ。従来は不自然な日本語や英語で見破られていたフィッシングメールも、大規模言語モデルを使えば自然な文面を瞬時に大量生成できる。さらに、音声や映像を模倣するディープフェイクを使った標的型の詐欺、マルウェアコードの作成補助、認証情報を狙う攻撃の自動化など、AIが攻撃の各段階を加速させていると指摘されている。攻撃の起点として、パスワードやIDが依然として狙われやすい弱点である点も変わっていない。

こうした状況に対し、ブログが重視しているとみられるのが、ID保護を軸とした多層的な防御だ。一般的な推奨策としては、フィッシング耐性の高い多要素認証やパスキーの導入、最小権限の原則に基づくアクセス制御、ゼロトラストの考え方に沿った継続的な検証などが挙げられる。MicrosoftはEntraやSecurity Copilotといった製品群を通じて、AIを防御側でも活用し、異常なサインインや不審な挙動を検知・自動対応する仕組みを提供している。攻撃にAIが使われる以上、防御側もAIで対抗するという構図が鮮明になりつつある。

同様の問題意識は他社も共有しており、GoogleやOpenAI、各セキュリティベンダーが脅威インテリジェンスの強化やAI悪用の監視に取り組んでいる。一方で、防御側のAI活用が誤検知や運用負荷、過度な依存といった課題を伴う可能性も否定できず、人による判断やプロセス整備と組み合わせることが現実的だと考えられる。

利用者にとって重要なのは、特定の製品の導入だけで安全が保証されるわけではないという点だ。AIによって攻撃の速度と規模が増している前提に立ち、ID管理の見直しや従業員教育、インシデント対応の準備を含めた継続的な備えが、先手を打つうえで欠かせないといえる。
a3d032e5da368cd8.bodyEn:
Artificial intelligence is changing the economics of cybercrime, lowering the skill threshold for attackers while increasing the speed and scale at which campaigns can be launched. A recent post on Microsoft's Source blog, drawing on guidance associated with the company's Entra identity platform, examines how adversaries are putting generative AI to work and outlines concrete steps that organizations and individuals can take to stay ahead of the threat.

The central argument is that AI does not necessarily invent new categories of attack so much as it accelerates and refines existing ones. Phishing emails that once contained tell-tale grammatical errors can now be generated in fluent, context-aware prose at virtually no cost. Attackers appear to be using large language models to research targets, draft convincing lures, translate messages into multiple languages, and automate parts of the reconnaissance process that previously required manual effort. The result is a higher volume of more polished attacks, which puts pressure on defenses that have historically relied on spotting obvious red flags.

Identity has become a focal point of this shift, which is why the discussion is framed around Entra, Microsoft's identity and access management suite. As organizations move workloads to the cloud, stolen or compromised credentials are frequently the entry point for intrusions, and AI-assisted social engineering makes credential theft easier to pull off at scale. Voice cloning and deepfake media add another dimension, enabling impersonation attacks in which a request that appears to come from a senior executive or trusted colleague is actually synthetic. Such techniques are likely to grow more common as the underlying tools become cheaper and more accessible.

The recommended defenses described in the post are largely consistent with established security best practices, reframed for an environment in which attacks move faster. Strong, phishing-resistant multifactor authentication is emphasized, with passkeys and hardware-backed credentials presented as more durable than one-time codes that can be intercepted or relayed. A zero trust posture, in which every access request is verified rather than assumed safe based on network location, is positioned as a foundational principle. Continuous monitoring, least-privilege access, and prompt patching remain core to reducing the attack surface that automated tooling can probe.

A notable theme is the use of AI on the defensive side, sometimes described as fighting fire with fire. Security vendors, including Microsoft, are embedding machine learning into threat detection to flag anomalous sign-ins, unusual data movement, and behavior that deviates from a user's normal pattern. Microsoft's Security Copilot, an assistant aimed at security operations teams, is part of this broader push to help analysts triage alerts and respond more quickly. The premise is that defenders need automation to match the tempo set by attackers, since human teams alone struggle to keep pace with the growing volume of signals.

For context, this guidance arrives amid wider industry concern about AI-enabled threats. Government agencies and security organizations have issued advisories on AI-assisted phishing and deepfakes, and competing platforms from companies such as Google and CrowdStrike have introduced their own AI-driven detection and response features. Microsoft also publishes threat intelligence through its research teams, which track nation-state and criminal groups experimenting with these tools. Taken together, these efforts suggest the security market is converging on a model in which AI is treated as both a risk to be managed and a capability to be deployed.

Practical advice for individuals tends to echo the organizational recommendations on a smaller scale. Skepticism toward unsolicited messages remains important even when they look professional, and verifying unusual requests through a second channel can defeat impersonation attempts. Enabling multifactor authentication, using a password manager, and keeping software updated continue to offer meaningful protection. The underlying point is that fundamentals still matter, and that AI raises the cost of neglecting them.

It is worth reading such vendor guidance with the understanding that it serves a promotional purpose alongside its educational intent, since the recommendations naturally point toward the company's own products. Even so, the core message reflects a broad consensus among security professionals: the tools available to attackers are evolving quickly, and organizations that strengthen identity protections, adopt zero trust principles, and integrate automated defenses appear better positioned to respond. Staying ahead, the post suggests, is less about a single product than about building resilient practices before an incident forces the issue.

fe014a96b2c33fd4.bodyJa:
調査会社Pew Researchが公表した最新の世論調査で、米国人の多くがAIの急速な進歩に不安を抱きながらも、日常的にAIチャットボットを利用している実態が明らかになった。普及と懸念が同時に進む状況を映す結果として注目される。

調査によれば、米国の成人の49%が少なくとも時折AIチャットボットを使っていると回答した。OpenAIのChatGPTやGoogleのGemini、AnthropicのClaudeといったサービスが相次いで登場し、検索や文章作成、プログラミング補助など幅広い場面で利用が広がっていることを裏付ける数字といえる。一方で、63%がAI技術の進歩は「速すぎる」と感じていると答えており、利用者の中にも不安を抱える人が少なくないとみられる。

この「使うが不安」という二面性は、近年のAIをめぐる世論調査で繰り返し確認されてきた傾向と重なる。生成AIは2022年末のChatGPT公開以降、わずか数年で一般消費者にまで浸透した。技術の進化スピードに対して、雇用への影響や誤情報の拡散、プライバシー、著作権といった社会的な議論や制度整備が追いついていないとの指摘もあり、こうした状況が不安の背景にある可能性がある。

各国の対応には温度差もある。EUは包括的な規制枠組み「AI Act」を成立させ、リスクに応じた規律を進めている。これに対し米国では連邦レベルでの統一的な法整備は限定的で、企業の自主的な取り組みや州ごとの対応に委ねられている面が大きい。今回の調査結果は、技術の普及が先行する一方で、利用者保護やガバナンスのあり方を求める声が根強いことを改めて示したものといえる。

Pewの調査はあくまで一時点の世論を切り取ったものであり、設問の文言や調査時期によって数値は変動しうる。ただ、AIが生活に深く入り込むほど、人々の期待と警戒が併存する構図はしばらく続くと見られる。企業や政策当局が透明性の確保や説明責任にどう応えていくかが、今後の信頼形成を左右しそうだ。
fe014a96b2c33fd4.bodyEn:
A new Pew Research Center survey suggests that Americans are simultaneously embracing artificial intelligence and growing wary of how fast it is changing. According to the poll, 49 percent of Americans now use AI chatbots at least occasionally, while 63 percent say the technology is advancing too quickly. The split matters because it captures a public mood that is neither purely enthusiastic nor reflexively hostile, but rather marked by routine use shadowed by unease.

The headline figures point to a gap between adoption and comfort. Nearly half of respondents report turning to tools such as conversational assistants for everyday tasks, a level of uptake that would have seemed improbable only a few years ago. Yet a clear majority believe the pace of development outstrips society's ability to absorb it. That tension—using a product while doubting the speed of its progress—is a recurring theme in surveys of emerging technologies, and it appears especially pronounced with generative AI.

Pew has tracked attitudes toward AI for several years, and its surveys generally draw on large, nationally representative samples designed to reflect the U.S. adult population across age, education, race, and political affiliation. While the topline numbers are useful, the underlying breakdowns often tell a richer story. In past Pew work, younger adults and people with higher levels of formal education have tended to report more frequent use of AI tools, and concern about specific harms has frequently coexisted with curiosity about potential benefits. Readers should treat any single statistic as a snapshot rather than a settled verdict, since wording, timing, and the broader news environment can all shift responses.

The context behind these numbers is a market that has moved rapidly. Since OpenAI released ChatGPT in late 2022, large language models have become a centerpiece of consumer software. Google offers Gemini, Anthropic markets Claude, Microsoft has woven Copilot into Windows and Office, and Meta has embedded its assistant across its social apps. Many of these tools are now bundled into products people already use, which helps explain why occasional use has climbed even among those who never sought out a standalone chatbot. Adoption, in other words, is increasingly passive as well as active.

That ambient presence may also feed the sense that AI is moving too fast. Features arrive through automatic updates, default settings, and integrations that are difficult to opt out of, which can leave users feeling that the technology is advancing around them rather than at their request. Concerns commonly cited in this area include the spread of misinformation, the reliability of AI-generated answers, data privacy, the effect on jobs, and the use of copyrighted material to train models. The persistence of so-called hallucinations, where systems produce confident but inaccurate output, is one technical reason trust remains limited even as capability improves.

The findings land amid an active policy debate. In the United States, regulation has been uneven, with state-level measures, agency guidance, and voluntary commitments from major developers filling the gap left by the absence of comprehensive federal legislation. The European Union's AI Act, which takes a risk-based approach to oversight, has become a reference point for lawmakers elsewhere. Survey results like these are likely to be cited by advocates on multiple sides, both by those urging guardrails and by companies arguing that public familiarity is growing.

It is worth noting what the data does not establish. A belief that AI is advancing too quickly does not necessarily translate into opposition to the technology, support for specific rules, or a refusal to use it; the same respondents may value the tools they use daily. Likewise, occasional use is a low bar that can include anything from drafting an email to testing a chatbot once. The numbers describe sentiment and behavior, not the actual rate of technical progress, which is harder to measure objectively.

Taken together, the survey reinforces a picture that has emerged across several recent studies: AI is becoming normalized in daily life faster than public confidence in it is solidifying. For developers, that suggests the challenge ahead is less about driving initial adoption and more about earning trust through reliability, transparency, and clearer choices for users. For policymakers, the persistence of unease, even among regular users, indicates that demand for oversight is unlikely to fade as the tools become more common.

785db63aaf5ea790.bodyJa:
米AI企業のAnthropicが、トランプ政権による突然の指示を受け、外国籍ユーザーに対する最新AIモデルの提供を一時的に遮断せざるを得なくなった。米メディアThe Vergeが報じたもので、不透明な輸出規制の解釈をめぐる混乱が、AI業界に新たな波紋を広げている。

報道によれば、Anthropicは今週、すべての外国人ユーザーへのアクセスを停止するよう命じられ、数日間にわたって新しいモデルの利用に支障が生じたという。同社はサービス復旧に向けて対応に追われたとされるが、規制の文言が曖昧で、どの利用者がどの範囲まで制限の対象となるのかが判然としないことが、混乱に拍車をかけている。

背景には、AIを国家安全保障上の重要技術と位置づける米政府の方針がある。米国はこれまで、先端半導体やAI開発向けの高性能GPUの対中輸出を段階的に制限してきた経緯がある。今回の動きは、規制の焦点がハードウェアから、クラウド経由で提供されるAIモデルやサービスそのものへと拡大しつつある可能性を示すものと見られる。

Anthropicは、OpenAIやGoogleと並ぶ生成AIの主要企業の一つで、対話型AI「Claude」シリーズを手がける。同社はAIの安全性を重視する姿勢を打ち出してきたが、米国を拠点とする以上、政府の輸出管理規則に従う必要がある。仮に同様の規制が他社にも適用されれば、グローバルに展開するAIサービス全体に影響が及ぶおそれがある。

今回の件で特に問題視されているのは、規制内容の不明確さだ。企業が法令を順守しようとしても、解釈の指針が乏しければ、過度にサービスを絞り込んだり、逆に意図せず違反したりするリスクが高まる。突然の命令によって、利用者が予告なくサービスを使えなくなる事態も生じうる。

AI技術の国際的な普及が進むなか、各国政府は安全保障と経済的競争力のバランスをどう取るかという難題に直面している。今回のAnthropicの事例は、政策の設計と現場での運用が追いついていない現状を浮き彫りにしたと言える。今後、規制の明確化を求める声が業界から強まる可能性がある。
785db63aaf5ea790.bodyEn:
